newsitem.title: USA: Atmos, United Cities have Illinois pact.
newsitem.headline: Atmos, United Cities have Illinois pact.

text.p: Atmos Energy Corp said Tuesday agreement has been reached with the staff of the Illinois Commerce Commission in filing a proposed order which, if approved by the commission, would grant approval of the merger of Atmos and United Cities Gas Co.
In April, the hearing examiner issued a proposed order recommending that the merger not be approved, Atmos said.

In November 1996, shareholders of both companies approved the merger in which Atmos would be the surviving entity. Regulatory approval is required in 10 of the 13 states in which the combined companies would operate.
To date, Atmos said, approvals have been received in all states requiring approval except Illinois.
The hearing examiner's order was based upon his finding that Atmos and United Cities had not submitted sufficient evidence to show the merger would have produced net benefits to Illinois customers.
United Cities and Atmos have now submitted a study which demonstrates such net benefits, and have agreed to pass those benefits on to the Illinois customers, the company said.

The proposed order, if accepted by the hearing examiner, can at the earliest be considered by the commission at its June 25 public meeting. Following commission approval, the parties would then have 30 days in which to seek rehearing. The parties to the proceeding are Atmos, United Cities and the commission staff.

Atmos Chief Executive Officer Robert W. Best said "We are still on target to close the merger by the end of July. We are confident that our settlement with the Illinois Commerce Commission staff will be approved by the commission later this month." ((-- New York Newsdesk 212-859-1610.))
